character.name: David
character.trait: trusting God when things look big

translation.name: World English Bible
translation.note: WEB renders God's name as "Yahweh". A church that prefers "the LORD" needs a display setting; not built yet.

ageNotes.explorer: Keep to two ideas: God chose David because of his heart, and God helped David be brave.
ageNotes.trailblazer: Add the lion and the bear (17:34-37), Saul's armour (17:38-39) and David's words to Goliath (17:45).

bigIdea: God looks at the heart, and God helps us be brave.

sensitivity.notes: Goliath is killed (17:49-50). For Explorers say the giant fell down and God's people were safe; do not dwell on it. If a child asks directly, answer honestly and briefly: the giant died, and God's people were safe. Trailblazers can hear the account as written.

preClass.teaser: Somebody in this story was the youngest in his family, and nobody thought he'd matter. Can you work out who?

clues: I was the youngest in my family.
I spent my days looking after sheep.
God chose me, even though nobody else expected it.
I faced a giant with a sling.

roles.storyteller: Tells the story. The only voice for the main narrative.
roles.coFacilitator: Runs chat and reactions, admits children from the waiting room, watches for anyone lost or upset.

part1.title: The shepherd boy
part1.retelling: God sent the prophet Samuel to a man called Jesse in Bethlehem, because God had chosen one of Jesse's sons to be the next king. Jesse's sons walked past one by one. They looked tall and strong, and Samuel thought, surely it's him. But God said no. Then Samuel asked, "Are all your children here?" There was one more: the youngest, out looking after the sheep. His name was David. They sent for him. God said, "This is the one." Samuel poured oil on David's head, and God's Spirit came on David from that day on.

quoted.text: But Yahweh said to Samuel, “Don’t look on his face, or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him; for I don’t see as man sees. For man looks at the outward appearance, but Yahweh looks at the heart.”

part1.prop: A shepherd's staff (or a walking stick).

part2.title: The giant
part2.retelling: Israel's army was camped on one hill and their enemies, the Philistines, on another. Every day a giant named Goliath walked out and shouted a challenge, and everyone in Israel's army was afraid. David had been sent by his father with food for his brothers, and he heard the giant. David said, "I'll go." King Saul said David was too young, but David told him how God had helped him against a lion and a bear while he looked after his sheep. Saul gave David his own armour, but it was too heavy and David took it off. David picked up his shepherd's staff, chose five smooth stones from the stream, and took his sling. He told Goliath he was coming in the name of the God of Israel. Then he ran towards the giant, put a stone in his sling, and the stone struck Goliath, who fell to the ground.
part2.explorerVersion: Everyone was scared of a giant called Goliath. But David wasn't. David remembered how God had helped him before, when he looked after his sheep. So David took his sling and five smooth stones. He didn't wear armour and he didn't have a sword. God helped David, and the giant fell down. God's people were safe.

quoted.text: David said, “Yahweh who delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.”

Then David said to the Philistine, “You come to me with a sword, with a spear, and with a javelin; but I come to you in the name of Yahweh of Armies, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.

part2.prop: A sling (or a rolled-up sock), and one smooth stone.

activities.prompt: Everyone stand up. When the leader says "sheep", crouch and go "baa". When the leader says "shepherd", stand tall and hold out a staff. Swap a few times, going faster.
Would you have gone out to face the giant? Show thumbs up, thumbs down, or a wobbly thumb. No wrong answers.
The leader answers as David while the children ask questions.
sampleQuestions: How did you feel when the giant shouted?
Why didn't you wear Saul's armour?
What did you remember about the lion and the bear?

activities.prompt: Find 1 Samuel 17:37 in your own Bible, or follow along on the leader's screen. Who does David say helped him before?
Draw a sling and one smooth stone on paper. Hold it up to the camera if you'd like to.
Open questions, no single right answer. Don't rush to a moral.
questions: I wonder which part of the story you liked best.
I wonder how David felt when he ran towards the giant.
I wonder where you are in this story.

mission.title: Brave for a day
mission.description: Do one brave or kind thing this week that you find a bit hard. Tell a grown-up, and they can confirm it on the hub.

familyQuestions: Who do people sometimes pick last? How could we show them that God sees their heart?

David remembered how God had helped him before. What is one time you remember God helping us?
